services.name: Drain Cleaning
services.h1: Drain Cleaning in Round Rock, TX
services.title: Drain Cleaning Round Rock, TX | Round Rock Plumbing Company
services.meta: Round Rock Plumbing Company clears slow, blocked, and backing-up drains in Round Rock, TX, with checks of traps, cleanouts, branches, and drain lines.
services.blurb: We clear slow, gurgling, and backing-up drains across Round Rock.

paragraphs: Water backing into a shower is a drain warning. A gurgling sink, standing water, or a sour odor near a floor drain can point to the same line.

A blockage may sit in the trap, branch pipe, or a cleanout farther along the route. Drain trouble should not be left alone because grease, soap, food, and hair can compact inside the pipe and turn a slow fixture into a backup.

sections.heading: Gurgling sinks and drain odors
paragraphs: We hear about sinks that drain only after several minutes, tubs that fill while the washing machine empties, and toilets that bubble when another fixture runs. Kitchen sinks may hold water under the basket strainer, while a shower can send water across the bathroom floor.

A sewer-like smell can come from a dry trap, trapped debris, or a blockage farther down the branch line. These symptoms can look alike from the room, but each fault has its own access, tools, and scope once we inspect the pipe.

sections.heading: Drain line inspection
paragraphs: We check the fixture, trap, branch line, and reachable cleanout before selecting a cable, auger, or water flush. We note whether a 1 1/2-inch sink line, 2-inch shower line, or larger main is involved.

A basic flow test and trap check take about 10 to 15 minutes. Clearing one accessible fixture line often takes under an hour, and we remove hair, soap, food residue, or grease where the blockage is reachable.

We can usually clear an accessible line and test its flow during the same visit. We replace a damaged trap washer or cleanout cap if inspection shows it is needed, while camera work, buried pipe work, or sewer line repair may need separate scheduling.

sections.heading: Cleanouts, pipe material, and access
paragraphs: An accessible cleanout near a kitchen or bathroom gives the cable a direct route. A buried, painted-over, or seized cleanout cap adds locating and opening work before the line can be cleared.

Grease in a kitchen branch, hair in a shower trap, and roots in an outdoor line need different tools and clearing time. Older cast-iron pipe can hold scale that catches debris again after a basic cable pass.

The pipe material, route, and need for a camera affect the scope. A nonstandard cleanout fitting or damaged trap piece may need to be ordered, and any permit or sign-off for pipe alteration is addressed before that work is scheduled.

sections.heading: Fixture location and cleanout
paragraphs: Before calling, note the room and fixture with the problem, such as the kitchen sink, hall bathroom tub, or laundry drain. Tell us whether water is standing now and which other fixture causes the backup.

If you can see a cleanout, describe where it sits and whether furniture, cabinets, or landscaping block access. For a kitchen sink, the garbage disposal make and model on its label can also help us identify the setup.

Keep any prior camera footage or plumbing invoice nearby if the line has backed up before. Call Round Rock Plumbing Company at (512) 882-1291 before a partial blockage packs tighter and sends wastewater back through the fixture.

services.name: Water Heater Repair
services.h1: Water Heater Repair in Round Rock, TX
services.title: Heater Repair - Round Rock Plumbing Company, Round Rock, TX
services.meta: Round Rock Plumbing Company handles water heater repair in Round Rock, TX, including no hot water, leaks, rumbling tanks, and faulty controls.
services.blurb: We diagnose no-hot-water, leaks, rumbling, and control faults in Round Rock.

paragraphs: Cold water at the shower and water reaching the hallway from a utility closet are both called a water heater problem. They point to different faults: one can involve a burner, element, control, or gas supply; the other can come from a valve, pipe joint, relief line, or tank.
We check both tank and tankless units in Round Rock, Brushy Creek, Windemere, and Wells Branch. We trace the fault at the heater before replacing a part.

No hot water without a leak can usually wait for a planned repair. Water at the tank, a gas smell, a hot relief line, or a tripped breaker should not wait, because a failed vessel, gas connection, or electrical component can worsen quickly.

sections.heading: No hot water or rumbling
paragraphs: No hot water may mean cold water at every faucet, or it may mean a shower that turns cold after several minutes. A pilot that will not stay lit, a clicking tankless unit, and a breaker that trips while an electric heater runs point in other directions.

Brown water from the hot side, popping or rumbling under the tank, and water from the temperature-and-pressure relief pipe need separate checks. A puddle at the top fittings is not the same fault as water coming through the tank base.

These symptoms can look alike from the hallway, but they come from separate parts and lead to different repair costs. We inspect the burner, element, valve, control, and tank before identifying the work.

sections.heading: Tank and burner callout
paragraphs: On a callout, we identify the fuel or electrical supply, read the model plate, and inspect the tank, burner chamber, heating elements, thermostat, vent, relief valve, and nearby pipe joints. We measure incoming water pressure, check hot-water temperature, and test voltage or ignition where the unit uses it.

A straightforward diagnostic check commonly takes 30 to 60 minutes. A loose connection, thermostat, element, igniter, or relief valve can often be addressed on the same visit if the matching part is available.
A corroded tank seam, inaccessible component, or part that must be ordered needs a return visit. We explain whether a tank replacement should be scheduled rather than attempting a short-term patch.

sections.heading: Anode age, closet access, shutoffs
paragraphs: The age and condition of the anode rod, gas control, elements, and relief valve affect the repair scope. Older fittings may have corrosion at threads or a seized drain valve, which adds removal work.

A heater in an open garage gives us different access than one in a tight closet, attic, or finished utility room. A shutoff that will not close can require water isolation beyond the heater connections.
A common stocked part keeps the repair contained. A discontinued control, specific tankless component, permit sign-off, or ordered manufacturer part changes the visit and may require a return.

sections.heading: Model plate and closet access
paragraphs: Find the model and serial number on the rating plate before you call. On a tank, the plate is usually on the outer jacket; on a tankless unit, it is often behind or beside the front cover.
Tell us the approximate age of the unit and whether it is gas, electric, or tankless. Note which room has no hot water and whether every hot faucet is affected.
Say whether water is running from the relief pipe, drain valve, top connections, or tank base. Let us know if the heater sits in a closet, attic, garage, or another space with a narrow access route.
Call Round Rock Plumbing Company at (512) 882-1291; a tank leak can spread through flooring and framing while the repair waits.

services.name: Leak Repair
services.h1: Leak Repair in Round Rock, TX
services.title: Leak Repair | Round Rock Plumbing Company | Round Rock, TX
services.meta: Round Rock Plumbing Company repairs pipe, faucet, and fixture leaks in Round Rock, TX, locating the source before water damages cabinets or walls.
services.blurb: Pipe, faucet, and fixture leak repair in Round Rock, TX.

paragraphs: A drip under the sink can soak a cabinet floor within a week. Over a month, water can swell particleboard, loosen flooring, and leave a stain on the wall below. A small pipe leak inside a wall can keep feeding moisture into insulation and framing through an entire season.

We trace the water back to its source, whether it is a supply line, valve, faucet connection, or drain fitting. Leak repair should not wait when water is active, because each day of moisture can damage the cabinet, drywall, or floor around the fitting.

sections.heading: Water under the sink
paragraphs: Customers often call about water under the kitchen sink, a wet spot on the ceiling, a faucet that drips after the handle is off, or a toilet area with water on the floor. Another common report is a water meter that moves while every fixture is off.

A puddle at a cabinet base may come from a supply tube, drain trap, shutoff valve, or faucet body. A ceiling stain may point to a bathroom fixture above it, but the pipe route can shift the water away from the actual opening.

These symptoms can look alike from the room, yet they come from different parts and require different repairs. We inspect the fitting and pipe rather than treating every drip or stain as the same fault.

sections.heading: Pipe inspection callout
paragraphs: We start by checking visible supply lines, shutoff valves, faucet connections, drain joints, cabinet floors, and nearby walls. We isolate fixtures where possible, watch the water meter, and measure system pressure. Residential water pressure commonly falls between 40 and 80 psi, and pressure outside that range can add strain to fittings.

A visible leak check often takes 20 to 40 minutes. We can usually replace an exposed supply tube, compression fitting, cartridge, or drain seal during the same visit if the correct part is available. A leak behind tile, inside a wall, or beneath a slab may need a separate visit for access work or a more involved repair.

sections.heading: Shutoff valves and wall access
paragraphs: The repair changes with the age and condition of the failed part. A worn faucet cartridge or accessible supply tube is different from a corroded valve, a cracked pipe, or a fitting hidden behind a finished wall.
Access also matters. A leak under an open vanity allows direct work, while a pipe behind tile, cabinetry, or drywall may require careful opening and restoration by the appropriate trade.

A seized shutoff valve can add work because the water supply must be controlled before a fitting comes apart. A specialty cartridge, older valve stem, or uncommon pipe fitting may need to be ordered. Some wall or pipe work can also require sign-off depending on the scope and location.

sections.heading: Fixture model and access
paragraphs: Before calling, note which room has the leak and which fixture is involved. Check whether water is running now, whether the cabinet floor is wet, and whether the main or local shutoff valve can still turn.

If the faucet or toilet has a brand name, find the model number on the plate, underside, tank, or installation paperwork. Tell us the approximate age of the fitting and whether the pipe is behind a wall, under a cabinet, or in a crawl space.
Clear items from beneath the sink or vanity if that is where water appears. Photos of the puddle, stain, valve, or supply line can also help identify the likely part.
Call Round Rock Plumbing Company at (512) 882-1291 before active water spreads through the cabinet, drywall, or flooring.

services.name: Toilet Repair
services.h1: Toilet Repair in Round Rock, TX
services.title: Toilet Repair | Round Rock Plumbing Company, Round Rock, TX
services.meta: Round Rock Plumbing Company repairs running, leaking, clogged, and weak-flushing toilets in Round Rock, TX, Brushy Creek, Windemere, and Wells Branch.
services.blurb: We fix running, leaking, clogged, and weak-flushing toilets in Round Rock.

paragraphs: We see a plunger as the sensible first tool for a bowl that will not clear. We expect homeowners to try a few steady plunges first, because paper can lodge in the trapway and then release.
We know a plunger has a limit when the bowl refills, the water level rises, or the blockage returns after every flush. A running tank or water at the toilet base needs a different repair than a clog.

We can schedule a toilet that has cleared and is flushing normally. A toilet that keeps running, leaks onto the floor, backs up, or will not flush should not wait because water can damage flooring and leave the fixture unusable.

sections.heading: Running water and weak flushes
paragraphs: We often hear, "My toilet keeps running," after the tank has refilled but water still moves through the overflow tube. We also hear, "The toilet will not flush," or, "It flushes but the bowl stays full."

We check for a weak flush that leaves paper in the bowl, a gurgling sound after flushing, and water around the base of the fixture. A toilet can also smell musty near the floor if a seal has failed or water has been sitting below the bowl.

We treat these as separate faults, even when they sound similar over the phone. A fill valve, flapper, flush valve, wax ring, trapway blockage, and loose tank bolt each need different parts and labor.

sections.heading: Fixture inspection and test
paragraphs: We start the fixture inspection by flushing the toilet, checking the bowl level, and watching the tank refill. We inspect the flapper, fill valve, overflow tube, supply line, shutoff valve, tank bolts, and base of the bowl.

We can use dye in the tank to find a flapper leak, and the test commonly takes about 15 minutes. We also check whether the tank water sits roughly 1 inch below the top of the overflow tube and may measure supply pressure, which is commonly kept between 40 and 80 psi in residential plumbing.

We can usually replace a standard flapper, fill valve, handle, or supply line during the same visit if the fitting matches available parts. A cracked bowl, damaged flange, seized hardware, or discontinued tank component may need a return visit after the correct part is located.

sections.heading: Fill valves, shutoffs, and access
paragraphs: The age of the fill valve, flapper, and flush valve affects the repair because older tank parts may be worn, brittle, or no longer matched to current replacements. A standard tank with an accessible lid is simpler to work on than a concealed carrier or a fixture set tight against tile.
The shutoff valve also matters. If the valve beneath the tank has seized or the supply line cannot be safely disconnected, the repair can extend beyond the parts inside the tank.

We also account for corroded tank bolts, a toilet that must be lifted to reach the flange, and any part that has to be ordered by model. Property-manager approval or required sign-off can add coordination before work on the fixture moves ahead.

sections.heading: Tank model numbers and shutoffs
paragraphs: We ask you to note which bathroom has the problem and whether the toilet is running, leaking, backing up, or failing to flush now. We also ask whether water is visible at the base, under the tank, or near the shutoff valve.

We can use a model number stamped inside the tank or printed on the underside of the tank lid to help match parts. We also benefit from the approximate age of the toilet and any tight access around the bowl or tank.
Call Round Rock Plumbing Company at (512) 882-1291 before a running fill valve keeps wasting water or a base leak damages the flooring beneath the toilet.

services.name: Water Heater Installation
services.h1: Water Heater Installation in Round Rock, TX
services.title: Water Heater | Round Rock Plumbing Company | Round Rock, TX
services.meta: Round Rock Plumbing Company installs water heaters in Round Rock, TX. We check tank access, valves, venting, and heater sizing before installation.
services.blurb: Water heater installation with tank, valve, venting, and access checks.

paragraphs: We hear, “The shower went cold,” “the tank is leaking,” or “the water looks rusty.” Those calls usually mean the water heater needs an inspection to determine whether a new unit is the right answer.

We check the tank, supply lines, drain valve, venting, and electrical or gas connections before planning an installation. A planned replacement can be scheduled, but a leaking tank should not wait because water can damage flooring, drywall, and nearby cabinets.

sections.heading: Cold showers and rusty water
paragraphs: People often call about no hot water at the shower, rusty water from a faucet, a rumbling tank, or a puddle beneath the heater. A gas unit may also make a clicking sound without lighting, while an electric unit may produce only lukewarm water.

Hot water that runs out sooner than usual can point to a worn heating element, a damaged dip tube, sediment in the tank, or a heater that no longer fits the household demand. A visible leak may come from a valve, a supply connector, or the tank shell itself.

These signs can look alike from the kitchen or bathroom, but the fault behind them changes the required parts, labor, and installation scope. We inspect the heater and its connections before identifying what needs to be replaced.

sections.heading: Tank inspection and hookup
paragraphs: At the tank inspection, we read the model plate, confirm the fuel type, and measure the heater space, doorway, and access route. We check the cold-water shutoff, hot-water outlet, drain valve, pressure relief valve, and the gas vent or electrical circuit.

We also test water pressure with a gauge and look for corrosion on supply lines and fittings. The inspection commonly takes about 20 to 40 minutes. A straightforward like-for-like tank replacement commonly takes two to four hours once the correct heater is on site.

We can often disconnect the old tank, set the new heater, reconnect approved fittings, and test hot water during the same visit. A job needing a new vent route, electrical work, a platform change, or permit sign-off may need a separate installation date.

sections.heading: Tank access and shutoff valves
paragraphs: Tank age, closet access, and the shutoff valve all affect the installation work. An older heater can have corroded connectors, outdated venting, or fittings that do not match a current replacement unit.

A heater in a tight closet, attic, garage corner, or upper-floor utility room may require more protection for walls, flooring, and the access path. A seized water shutoff can add work before the old tank can be removed safely.

The replacement unit itself also matters. Gas vent material, electrical connections, drain-pan needs, and a required inspection or sign-off can change the materials and work needed for the installation.

sections.heading: Model plate and closet access
paragraphs: Find the model number on the rating plate attached to the side of the water heater. The plate also shows the fuel type, capacity, and electrical or gas specifications.
Tell us the room where the tank sits and whether it is in a closet, attic, garage, or utility room. Let us know if water is running from the tank, the pressure relief valve, or a nearby pipe.

A photo of the heater, vent pipe, and doorway can help us plan for the right replacement and access equipment. Call Round Rock Plumbing Company at (512) 882-1291 before a tank leak spreads into the floor, wall, or cabinet.

services.name: Sewer Line Repair
services.h1: Sewer Line Repair in Round Rock, TX
services.title: Sewer Repair | Round Rock Plumbing Company, Round Rock, TX
services.meta: Round Rock Plumbing Company repairs damaged sewer lines in Round Rock, TX, with camera inspection, locating, and repair planning for backups and odors.
services.blurb: Camera-led sewer line repairs for backups, odors, and damaged pipe in Round Rock.

paragraphs: Older homes in Round Rock and Brushy Creek can still have cast-iron, clay, or Orangeburg sewer pipe beneath the yard or slab. These materials can crack, shift at joints, or lose their shape as soil moves and roots enter the line.
Newer properties can also develop trouble at a pipe connection, cleanout, or low section of the yard line. We inspect the pipe route and the fixtures affected before recommending repair work.
A damaged sewer line should not be left for later. A crack or separation can release wastewater into soil, bring sewage through a floor drain, and allow a backup to spread farther through the home.

sections.heading: Sewage smell and yard puddles
paragraphs: Customers often call about a sewage smell near the bathroom, a wet patch in the yard, or water bubbling from a cleanout cap. Other common reports include toilets that gurgle after flushing and a tub or shower that fills with dirty water.

A backup in one fixture can point to a blockage, but repeated trouble across several fixtures often involves the main line. Soft ground above the pipe can also signal a broken joint, though irrigation and rainwater can look similar.

These signs can come from different faults, including root entry, a cracked pipe, a separated fitting, or a section that has sunk. They can look alike from indoors, but the labor, materials, and repair scope change once we inspect the line.

sections.heading: Camera inspection and locating
paragraphs: We start at the cleanout when one is available and run a sewer camera through the pipe. The camera shows root masses, cracks, standing water, offset joints, and collapsed sections that are not visible from the bathroom or yard.

An initial camera inspection and surface locating commonly takes 30 to 60 minutes. We check the pipe diameter, mark the approximate route, and identify the distance to the damaged area using the camera counter and locator.

A loose cleanout cap or accessible fitting may be replaced during the same visit. Excavation, under-slab pipe work, or repairs requiring ordered fittings are planned as a separate job after the damaged section is located.

sections.heading: Pipe depth and cleanout access
paragraphs: Pipe material changes the repair plan. PVC can often be cut and coupled at the damaged section, while aging cast iron, clay, and Orangeburg pipe may have failures beyond the first visible break.
Access also affects the work. A cleanout beside an open yard gives us a different route than a line below concrete, landscaping, a fence, or a driveway.

A deep pipe run, roots around the line, and a blocked or damaged cleanout can add work before the pipe is reached. Permit requirements, inspection sign-off, and special-order fittings can also extend the scope of a sewer repair.

sections.heading: Cleanout location and pipe material
paragraphs: Before calling, check whether you can find the sewer cleanout in the yard, garage, utility room, or near the exterior wall. Let us know which fixtures back up, including toilets, tubs, showers, or floor drains.

If sewage is still moving through a drain, tell us where it appears and whether the problem follows laundry, showers, or flushing. A prior camera report, repair invoice, or note about PVC, cast iron, or clay pipe can help us bring suitable fittings.

Tell us about gates, locked side yards, concrete, or landscaping above the suspected pipe route. Call Round Rock Plumbing Company at (512) 882-1291 before a sewer backup spreads through another drain or floor fixture.
